request.text: The paginated search endpoint drops results. With 7 matches and a page size of 3 the API reports 2 pages, so page 3 is never requested and the last match is never shown. `paginate()` also returns one item too few on every page. Find the cause and fix it. `npm test` reproduces it.

containment.writeContainmentNote: Claude Code 2.1.260 has no OS sandbox. Executed proof: a SessionStart hook the runtime itself launched wrote outside every granted directory, wrote to /tmp, read a file outside them and reached https://example.com — under `--restricted --permission-mode plan --permission-prompts none` as well as without them. What the flags do bound is the *tool surface* offered to the model (verified: `--restricted --tools …` yields exactly the named tools), which is a permission boundary, not a containment boundary. A kernel-level boundary must come from the environment around the process

unenforceable.reason: Claude Code has no OS sandbox: it bounds what its own tools will do, not what the processes it starts may do. A SessionStart hook launched by the installed 2.1.260 build wrote outside every granted directory, wrote to /tmp, read outside and reached the network (docs/runtime-claude-code.md, "Containment truth"). Kernel-level containment must come from the environment around the process.
no flag on this build denies worker-tool network access. `--restricted` removes WebFetch from the tool set unless --tools names it, which is a tool-surface reduction, not a network boundary.
no flag prevents a worker from attempting a push or a deployment; the coordinator denies external delivery by withholding credentials and remotes, not through this adapter.

evidence.containmentNote: THIS RUN HAD NO ENFORCED WRITE BOUNDARY. the claude-code adapter reports write_containment "unsupported" for 2.1.260 on darwin: nothing outside the runtime's own tool permissions bounds where a process it starts may write. Claude Code 2.1.260 has no OS sandbox. Executed proof: a SessionStart hook the runtime itself launched wrote outside every granted directory, wrote to /tmp, read a file outside them and reached https://example.com — under `--restricted --permission-mode plan --permission-prompts none` as well as without them. What the flags do bound is the *tool surface* offered to the model (verified: `--restricted --tools …` yields exactly the named tools), which is a permission boundary, not a containment boundary. A kernel-level boundary must come from the environment around the process It ran under an explicit --allow-unconfined-writes, so writes outside the granted candidate were possible and were not prevented; the file changes listed above are what the runtime reported, not what a boundary permitted. The candidate workspace is a linked Git worktree: development isolation, not a security sandbox. Neither installed runtime confines reads at all — a worker can read files outside the repository, and this run did not prevent that. Each check ran in a separate disposable copy of the frozen candidate under a sanitized environment, but with this user's own filesystem privileges: repository test code could still read or write anything this user can, including the coordinator state root. An enforced execution boundary for tool and test subprocesses (FR042) is an R1 gate; acceptance compensates only by refusing evidence whose fixtures the candidate changed.
